Schleich Horse Club 70-Piece Lakeside Country Dollhouse and Horse Stable Playset for Kids Ages 5-12 This box was heavy!
The quality of the pieces is exceptional.
The house and barn come together quickly and easily. They click together and they can easily be separated by pushing on the tabs if you wanted to take it apart.
I cannot attest to the durability of the horses legs, which were packaged with cardboard between them, which worried me that they might be fragile. Time will tell on that.
But the structure itself is very stable. There are SO MANY accessories. The house has specific locations where the picture sticker is added to the wall and the ribbons get added to the wall, etc.
I was surprised by the amount of details.
I love the attic hatch in the floor and the telescope in the attic. The only thing I think it is missing is a third person. The family photo that comes with it has four people in the family. The bedrooms can fit four people. Also, I do wish that all the people could ride the horses and not just the one person.
It would be nice if two people were included that could ride a horse so it would be easier to have so siblings or friends play together. The saddle is elaborate.
My 10 year old niece thought this was really neat and was excited to play with it.
My almost 5 year old nephews were excited to play with it also, they like to play with the farm set that is at a 1:64th scale, I was kind of expecting these to be at that scale, but it is much bigger.
Schleich is very high quality brand for miniatures and has a good reputation for that reason.
I guess I'll have to buy a few more kits to get a rider and another kid for the family.

text_fidelity_a:
Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd Comes packed in a nice sturdy box. Inside the play yard is in a nice nylon bag.
Just pull the 2 velcro straps open, take off the wrap around/bottom part of play yard, pop the play yard open, insert bottom pad.
It wasn't until I was packing this back up that I found the instructions. They are in a small pocket that's on the wrap around/bottom pad part of play pen. With that said, we had a little trouble getting this set up but, finally got it figured out without instructions.
When opening, before you push the middle part of the bottom down, straighten and lock the side rails up. If you open it up all the way, the two smaller sides won't lock into place. Pull the red strap back up a bit then click them and push the bottom back down.

The bottom pad is a bit thin and it's a little shorter than the play yard is. Nothing that I would take a star away for.
Once set up, it seems sturdy enough to keep a small child safe.
There is nice padding around the entire top. Even the release buttons are under the padded top rail so there's no chance of child pinching any fingers.
Has nice plastic wheels on one side so you can easily lift one side and roll it to another location.
The top arching top attachment is cute with 2 small monsters attached to it. It just snaps onto the side rails and is nice and flexible. Not sure how much abuse that can withstand. And not sure what a bigger child would do to it if they were jumping in it.
Packing it back up was just a little difficult. Have to make sure the side rails are completely released so it closes up nicely to be packed. Nothing to complain about. Do it a few times and it will be a breeze.
The bottom pad wraps around the play yard. Put velcro straps through opening, pull tight, and push the velcro into place.
Slips back easily into nylon packing bag.
Nylon bag also has a couple handles for easy carrying and I can slip it onto a bike hook and hang it in the garage so it doesn't take up floor space.
This is a great play pen/play yard for a young child. Can toss it into the car and bring it anywhere you might need it.
I think the price is a great price for what you're getting.
I really don't have any complaints with this.
text_fidelity_b: Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd

text_fidelity_a:
World Series of Yahtzee Board Games [[VIDEOID:9706f008dc0f922f2a22889963de0e00]] This is a digital, board-based game of Yahtzee. I think it's made to compete with [[ASIN:B0042ET8S0 Uno Attack Game]] and [[ASIN:B001G5431A Bunco]], and it is much more fun than both of those games. Sometimes making a classic into a digital version is a mistake, but the designers did an awesome job with this game.

It's still [[ASIN:B00000IWH6 Yahtzee]]. You still get five dice, and you have to match the classic Yahtzee combinations of Yahtzee (five of a kind), four of a kind, three of a kind, full house, small straight (sequence or run) and large straight. But, everybody plays at once with their own sets of five dice, and the computer in the middle moderates everything, so goes very quickly and it's exciting.

The little buzzer in the middle is pretty sophisticated for a simple computer. It records who buzzes in and in which order you buzzed in, and it plays some fun countdown music. You get five seconds after the first person finishes to finish rolling and to buzz in yourself. Each person can collect up to one card per turn, based on what they rolled, but if you're not lucky, or if someone else gets your combination first, then you don't get any cards per turn. Usually turns take about thirty seconds each, and a full game all the way through will take about ten minutes, so it's very fast paced and fun.

I really liked the original Yahtzee, and I really like this too.

Pros:
+Very fun new version of an already fun classic
+Doesn't waste paper like the old version
+No more waiting around for slow players, like the old version
+You really should start playing this instead of Bunco, since there's a lot more strategy in this game
+You can roll the dice as many times as you want, where in traditional Yahtzee, you could only roll the dice three times per turn

Cons:
-The black dice with the red dots are so much cooler than the rest of the dice, so everyone will be fighting over these
-Made out of cheap plastic cardboard. If you love this game, which you probably will, and if you're not a dainty family, which you probably aren't, then you'll break these pretty quickly and go through about one of these games per year. It's still cheaper than a night at the movies, though, and this game is fun enough to justify getting a new one.
text_fidelity_b: World Series of Yahtzee Board Games

-Putting this track together takes some time, so make sure you set aside a bit of time. I hate to admit it probably took me 30 minutes or so to figure things out. The directions weren't super clear, so it did take a bit of trail and error. I still ended up with 3 extra (small) pieces, and I couldn't figure out where they went. The part that moves never would line up properly, so the train would just fall back down the hill. My husband would have to sit and hold that part up every time the train came to it in order for it to work. Those extra parts could have possibly made a difference with that problem, but again, I couldn't figure out where they went.

-Also, the train requires 2 AAA batteries, which are NOT included.

Overall, just like all the other Thomas train tracks we have, this one was fun. I DO hope that we eventually get the track error corrected, though. Once we figure out those extra parts, I believe we will.
text_fidelity_b: Thomas & Friends TrackMaster, Avalanche Escape Set

Ontel Magic Tracks The Amazing Racetrack That Can Bend, Flex and Glow - As Seen On TV Multicolor, 11' Like many people, I have seen this product advertised on television and was excited to see if it is as fun as it looks in the commercials. The set comes with 1 car, a sheet of stickers to decorate the car, and 20 track segments in four different colors. The car requires 2 AAA batteries that are NOT included. The track segments are made of small individual pieces, which is why the box says it comes with 220 pieces of track.

The track is flexible and can be arranged in many different ways, and each segment can be used as a straight or curved part of the track. The car worked well and stayed on the track. A small pamphlet with quick trips is included with ideas on making the track more fun. I used the cardboard pieces used to package the car to create a small ramp and tunnel which worked better than I expected. After the track pieces were exposed to bright light, they did slightly glow in the dark. However, the box shows a picture of a looped track. I tried both a couple types of loops and none of them worked because the flexible track wouldn't support the weight of the car. In spite of this, this is a fun racetrack set that allows for a lot of different track formations to keep kids interested.

Willking Pyramid Speed Cube 3x3x3 Pyraminx Speed Cube Triangle Puzzle Magic Cube This brought back many memories for me. I was a kid of the 80s, when the original Rubik's Cube came out. My parents were poor, so I could not get a genuine Rubik's Cube, but I got a knock off brand for Christmas that year. I have always been one of those brainy kids who likes mentally stimulating puzzles, games, and toys. My friends had these Pyraminx puzzles shortly after the Rubik's Cube came out and I have always wanted one. Now I have one.

This one is very nice. It turns easily and has bright, attractive colors. It is just the right size for my hands. I'm also quirky in that I like the box that it came in. It has illustrated instructions on how to solve, in Chinese, and a picture of a satisfied young man holding an acutal cube shaped cube on one side. He looks happy with himself so I guess this was fun for him. Or maybe he was saying, "I expected a pyramid one but a cube one came out of the box." Since I cannot read Chinese, I can only use my imagination about what this young man is saying about it. ETA I found out the man on the side of the box is the world record Rubik's Cube solving champion.

Back to the cube, this was a fun and nostalgic blast from the past. It was easy for me to solve. This is perfect for any child or adult who loves puzzles, challenges, or who fiddles a lot. It also makes an attractive and colorful desktop display. All in all, no complaints. It's great for any age.

text_fidelity_a: LeapFrog Fridge Phonics Magnetic Letter Set, Pink I used LeapFrog Fridge Phonics when my children were little. Back then, it came with big chunky letters you'd press in to hear, "S says sss, S says sss. Every letter makes a sound. S says sss." (Or whatever letter you set in place). It also played the ABC song when you pressed the music note. We also had the Word Whammer that let you spell three letter words. The magnets were interchangeable and increased learning fun. Since then, I've always purchased LeapFrog products for the wee ones in the family. When I saw LeapFrog now had an adorable bus, I had to have it for my niece. It comes with the 26 letters of the alphabet and does everything the original LeapFrog did plus has some extra bonuses. Instead of just singing the ABC song, Leap sings two additional songs. He also uses the letters to create words and puts it in a sentence. (It's almost like having the Fridge Phonics and Word Whammer in one.) So not only is your child learning their alphabet, they are also learning how letter sounds work together to create words and complete sentences. The only downside of this darling phonics bus is the size of the letters. They used to be much larger.

text_fidelity_a: Intex Swim Center Family Inflatable Pool, 90" X 90" X 22", for Ages 6+, Color may vary I got the older version of this  (without the clear panels) two years ago, but it popped when my son cannonballed into the side, pushing it into a bolt on the swing. We have used this one for three days straight and no problems (a thunderstorm with potential for hail had us deflating it and putting it up for now).  We never fill to the line because the weight of the water and the splashing my two kids (6 and 9) make mean the sides bulge and I don't want to risk a seam failure.  The picture makes it look bigger than it is, the indents are pretty big and mean it is not 9'x9' on the inside, more like 8'x8'.  The three ribs of the side are all inflated with one valve...so if you do spring a leak it is going to be tough to find it, and you will lose all your water.  (Our last one had three tubes, so if it started to leak you only lost one "rib" and had a chance to fix it before all the water was lost.  And the vinyl is not industrial thick.  But for the price, we love it.  I don't leave inflatable pools out for more than three days at a time, and it is put on a level surface with a tarp and foam mat underneath so that might be why we get ours to last for several seasons...
text_fidelity_b: Intex Swim Center Family Inflatable Pool, 90" X 90" X 22", for Ages 6+, Color may vary

text_fidelity_a:
Minsk Remote Control Stunt Car Toy, 4WD RC Cars Double Sided Rotating Vehicles 360° Flips to Bloom, 2.4GHz High Speed Rechargeable Toy Presents for 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 Year Old Boy Birthday The car itself is pretty cool. I like the way it moves its entire axels to do its stunts. You can get a pretty good idea of hwo this moves if you look at the pictures. Simple, but effective. Seems like kids younger than 8 would like this; odd because they show small kids crawling on the floor using this, but say it is for ages 8 and up. Just watch they don't try to eat the batteries, I guess. It's not super fast, either, so older kids might get bored.

Anyway, they totally cheaped out on the battery setup. 400mAh?!?! Are you kidding me? Even the cheap, "included" versions of decent brands are 1100mAh, with good ones getting 2500mAh or more. And why the goofy charging setup? You have to take it out and then hook it to an oddball USB cable (so now you can't just use any USB cable you have laying around, you have to have this one on hand). They should just wire a higher capacity battery inside and add a micro-USB port like everybody else. And maybe similar functionality for the controller, which, oddly, uses two batteries...more than the car itself.

Pretty fun. Not well thought out overall, but on the other hand, if your kids falls out of love with toys quickly, maybe it's better not to spend more for the battery setup that could have been...
text_fidelity_b: Minsk Remote Control Stunt Car Toy, 4WD RC Cars Double Sided Rotating Vehicles 360° Flips to Bloom, 2.4GHz High Speed Rechargeable Toy Presents for 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 Year Old Boy Birthday

text_fidelity_a:
Tenergy TB6-B Balance Charger Discharger 1S-6S Digital Battery Pack Charger for NiMH/NiCD/Li-PO/Li-Fe Packs LCD Hobby Battery Charger w/ Tamiya/JST/EC3/HiTec/Deans Connectors + Power Supply 01435 This unit comes with almost everything you need to --

-- charge your LiPo's rapidly
-- balance charge your LiPo's so each cell has the same voltage
-- discharge your LiPo's if they're fully charged but you want to store them
-- charge your LiPo's to storage voltage levels for long term storage
-- plug your charger into AC wall power

The adapter cable fits a large variety of cell terminal plugs.

There is a balance port that receives the included balance plug adapter that can connect to anything up to 8S batteries.

This particular kit comes with an AC power supply like those that come with computers. The charger is really designed to hook to a car battery or other 12VDC high amperage source. This AC supply lets you plug it in at home easily and reliably. It comes with the right plug to fit perfectly.

The only things that could be added are extension cables on the balance connector to make it easier to charge the cells by making all the wires about the same length. [[ASIN:B00JBP32A0 JST JST-XH 3S Balance Wire Extention 20cm adapter 11.1v LiPo Battery Cable Li-Po]] This also allows you to put the cells into a fireproof bag during charging. [[ASIN:B005Q3VSZC Bluecell Black Medium Size Lipo Battery Guard Sleeve/Bag for Charge & Storage]]

One other accessory that really helps is a compact voltage indicator [[ASIN:B003Y6E6IE Integy C23212 Lipo Voltage Checker/Warning Buzzer]] that you plug into the balance port on the battery. Not strictly needed for recharging, but is very useful to monitor voltage after charging.

You'll need to consult YouTube for useful instructions on how to manipulate the four buttons and why, unless you want to read the manual. And who reads manuals anymore when a good ten minute video is clearer and simpler?

text_fidelity_a:
Holy Stone HS270 GPS 2.7K Drone with FHD FPV Camera Live Video for Adults, Portable Selfie Quadcopter with 2 Batteries for Beginners with Auto Return Home, Custom Flight Path, Follow Me, Auto Hover [[VIDEOID:bf921d7e8b73b1b75b44b485dab75323]] So after a week of having this unit I had 9 flights and was pleased to fly it! Although I had an issue once don't know if that was just the bird or that was me, I'm leaning toward me as I might have not turned the drone in the right direction and had a failure to calibrate or that could been just the area I was in and its inability to gain GPS, with that said it was pretty much a problem free week of flying the 270. Now dealing with the single battery was an issue, I do think they should offer a package or drone deal with 2 batteries standard. 😁.

I will say it is a great beginner drone for young teens are adults that want to get into flying. From the moment I unboxed it it felt great in my hands it didn't feel cheap most of the construction was plastic but with that said it is very consistent with some of the quality that I've become accustomed to with the hs700 the hs190 and a hs720. The controller is smaller then what I'm used to. It felt good in the hand but a lil small for my liking as I used my Galaxy Note 9 which is the limit as far as the holder, every other feature like the FPV, follow me mode and plotting way points , and circle point of interest on a map and it's going there and coming back worked pretty well. The Return too home when low on Battery functioned well as I flew the bird too that point almost everytime, there was an issue with the follow me I should have had it up a little higher it did hit a branch on a tree which was my fault because these drones do not come with obstacle avoidance and it took a fall to the ground no worse for wear I stopped the motors flipped back over unlock the motors and she went right back up no issues. Photo quality really really love the camera and take some great pictures even out that 400 ft. I really like the 4K camera and the quality of the video and pictures ( all photos post are unedited) and this unit also allows you to record record audio which is pretty good for bloggers , though my one gripe is I wish the 270 came with a gimbal to really make exceptional video, but at this price point it's a trade off!

The HS270 is very very wind resistant I flew this in pretty high winds somewhere between 15 to maybe 18 miles an hour and some strong gusts I thought for sure it going to blow over the pond or even into some of the trees. The GPS worked awesome as it kept the unit in its place and even though in my video it was shaky because you could see the wind is blowing it all over the place I was thoroughly impressed and this bird should not fly away from you unless you accidentally turn off the GPS in which case you really need to know how to fly this thing or any drones in the wind with the GPS off. It has a 3-speed future from low medium to high I enjoyed that it seemed like when it was windy I kicked it in high speed and it flew alot better keeping in medium most of the other times I enjoy a quick flights back and forth but was able to enjoy the roughly 21 minutes of flying time at the most and less on that really windy day it was only about 16 minutes most of the time it was fighting the wind. It takes pretty good pictures fpv to the cell phone like 720pvideo and 2K photo But the quality really comes to life when you have a SD card in the unit.

I think overall this unit does exactly as it's advertised to do and being able to fold up you can actually take this thing with you on vacation put in your suitcase carry out with you when you go on a hike and have something with you besides your camera that you can put up into the air and taking it up sectional a different view all of your vacation or a picture of you and your family or significant other standing by a Mountain or even the Grand Canyon with a drone from a distance and capture something that cant be done with a selfie stick. So I recommend this unit, but make sure you get extra batteries cuz it does take a while with the USB plug to charge the battery, most times it took 2-3 hours till fully charged. I grabbed a case on Amazon which I believe it was a case setup for a DJI mavic I did a little modifying on the sides of the hard foam and it was able to sit down in the case well which I showed the picture in the reviews it was the soyan case for like 22 bucks or something like that. All in all a great deal, I'm totally satisfied!
text_fidelity_b: Holy Stone HS270 GPS 2.7K Drone with FHD FPV Camera Live Video for Adults, Portable Selfie Quadcopter with 2 Batteries for Beginners with Auto Return Home, Custom Flight Path, Follow Me, Auto Hover

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

The packaging indicated Callie is from Japan, and she definitely has more almond-shaped eyes than Meredith. Her light skin, brown hair (instead of black), and eye shape reminded my bi-racial girls of themselves. That is the true gift of doll lines that have unique face sculpts, to provide a mirror so all little girls can have a doll that resembles them, as well as a truly diverse line of dolls.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Callie

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Speed Champions Lamborghini Urus ST-X and Lamborghini Huracán Super Trofeo EVO 76899 Building Kit (663 Pieces) I built this kit with my very LEGO-experienced 6-year-old, who found it to be just a little too challenging for her to do on her own (note that the box says 8+, but she has put together many 8+ kits on her own). Overall, I found this to be a fun little kit to put together, even though I'm not exactly a car guy. One of the models looks like a traditional black Lamborghini, while the other looks almost like an SUV in comparison, but it's probably jus the scale and the boxiness of the LEGO kits that makes me think this. In addition, you get a starting line that shifts left and right to give you green or red lights, which is a nice little added benefi.

The ads for this one talk about racing the cars, but it's all imaginary - there's no pull-back action or anything like you can get in Tecnic models - and the two included minifigs are basic to the point of being disappointing. Most of the pieces in this one are very small, and there's not much movement in the final models at all. Many of the other bigger pieces have decals, so there's limited use in terms of using this to build other models.

If you have a little car fan at home, this will thrill them. We're not car people, so we thought it was only just a bit better than OK.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Speed Champions Lamborghini Urus ST-X and Lamborghini Huracán Super Trofeo EVO 76899 Building Kit (663 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a: KINGBOT DeXop Rc Cartoon Car Cartoon Race Car with Music Radio Control Toy Action Figure Rc Vehicle for Toddler, CR04 [[VIDEOID:3cfc56c5d4bf143f7ccc504487426748]] My nephew gets freaked out if his Fischer Price remote control car moves his direction, and he's a brave little kid.  That car goes fairly slowly.  This thing flies and is NOT a toddler toy.  There's no way I'm putting the remote control in the hands an 18 mos. old, even as smart as he is!  The remote offers very little control and that's risky when you have something moving that fast around the floor.  The car doesn't stay on a straight path either.  While moving forward it veers left and right at random and moving backwards is crazy.  The colors are vibrant enough to get a child's attention.  The buttons you push to play sounds are easy to work.  Those are the steering wheel, the driver, and the top of the car.  Pressing the steering wheel causes the cute sound of a car cranking, revving its engine, and rumbling while idle.  The top button causes the weirdest, most random song I've ever heard on a child's toy and it goes on for a solid 36.40 seconds.  Yes, I timed it for this review.  It's that weird a song. When the driver is pressed, the car emits an odd vocalization that sounds like a cross between a dog barking and a man shouting "hey! Hey hey hey! Heeey!" (like something one might hear at the end of a nice Latin dance song) in an odd singsong voice.  The headlights flash whenever a button is pushed and do so for the entirety of whatever sound is playing.  The driver is detachable and once it's pressed down well, it takes some force to get it out.  The overall look of the car and remote is cute, like any regular toddler toy should be.  For an older child who knows how to handle a faster paced remote control car, the price is fair.  As a so called toddler toy...no way am I putting this anywhere near a small child.
text_fidelity_b: KINGBOT DeXop Rc Cartoon Car Cartoon Race Car with Music Radio Control Toy Action Figure Rc Vehicle for Toddler, CR04

text_fidelity_a:
Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets This word game is for 3 – 5 players. It’s for ages 10 and up. Takes 30-minutes to play.

It comes in a cardboard box measuring just under 10” X 6.25” X 2.25”. It’s part of the United States Playing Card company, which makes Bicycle playing cards. Made in China.

Each player receives chips, totaling 30-points, to start. You also receive two cards. From there you go around and each person “pays” for additional cards. Cards with letters which are worth more. . . cost more. You go around four-times. At the end, everyone turns-over their cards and you have thirty-seconds to spell a word with the most points. Please Note: Timer not included. Whomever wins that round gets chips equaling the number of points for their winning word. Then the second place person receives chips worth their number and so on. After playing three times, the person with the most points wins.

FYI. . . This came was originally going to be called “The World Series of AlphaBets”. . . but somewhere along the way they changed it to “Fumbling Ferrets”, probably to make it sound more “family friendly”. But it has nothing to do with ferrets.

If you like word / spelling games, then this one is fairly easy and fast to play. If you’re playing with younger kids, especially to start, you may wish to extend the timer to come-up with a word by a little bit and then shorten it with each round.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Fumbling Ferrets

text_fidelity_a:
Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up It's an 80s themed box, with a name like "Flashback" that has nothing to do with the 80s, and very little to do with "flashbacks". It's actually about werewolves, a magic ring, and bad poetry. The story makes no sense at all, and that's the easiest element of an escape room, really. Fortunately, everything else in this box is pretty good.

We played with a group of 4 people, which was perfect. You could even do six and have a great time with it. The game is broken into three paths - red, purple and blue, each with a very vague theme like "poems" (blue), "childhood" (purple) and "dinosaurs" (red) - and you need to complete all three in order to win. We broke our group of four into two teams of two and tackled blue and purple envelopes separately, then worked together on the red and the final puzzle. Each envelope took us roughly the same amount of time to beat, and the final puzzle was appropriately paced to be solved quickly. Most other escape room games we've played, from Unlock to Exit to Escape the Room all suffer from pacing problems, or narrowing you down to having only one puzzle or a few cards to work with at one time, which is nice for pointing out the way to solve some more complex puzzles, but which makes it rather difficult to play with more than two people - this box has solved that problem.

Overall, we were pretty impressed with this with a few caveats. One of the puzzles requires you to do something to the game pieces that is spelled out early on in the letter. It wasn't difficult to figure out what to do, but it was difficult to execute. It's hard to say more without giving out spoilers for one of the "coolest" puzzles in the box, but let's just say that it was mechanically difficult to work with. One of the puzzles at the end of the game required another outside prop that's easy to deal with, but the amount of finagleing with the pieces and the prop left us questioning if we had solved that puzzle correctly (we did, but it wasn't quite clear).

One touch that I particularly liked was how the game color-coded everything according to the paths/envelopes, and how the locked boxes worked - they performed exacly as they should have, and they were high enough quality that we felt like we could toss them around a little without any issues.

This is expensive for a one-time-use product, but it's definitely my favorite of the escape room games for a medium to large sized group, and it's probably pretty good for two slueths to solve on their own as well.

Solved in 1:07:11.
text_fidelity_b: Escape Room in a Box: Flashback, Escape Room Game with 19 Puzzles and 4 Locks, Can Pair with Amazon Alexa, For Adults and Teens 13 Years Old and Up

Water Marbling Paint Kit Arts and Crafts for Girls & Boys Christmas Thanksgiving Gifts for Kids Ages 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 This is a fun little marbling kit. Great way to test out how marbling works without investing a lot. Comes with a few sheets of paper, tray, paints, and thickening agent.
The instructions are very basic...too basic. They say to add the carrageenan to water and wait (appx 3 hours) for it to dissolve. But it didn't. It just sat on the surface. Even with mixing it just stayed glopped in the water. I had to do a bit of internet research to figure out how to actually dissolve it. Lots of prep time involved before you can actually use so plan accordingly. Also a little mix goes a long way and can be stored for a week, so this kit can make a decent amount if the solution even though it only comes with 8 sheets of paper
Once we had the solution everything else worked fine. We enjoyed experimenting with colors, placements and designs with the marbling paint. Very fun once you know what to do and get everything ready!

Patchwork | Strategy / Puzzle Game | Family Board Game | Two Player Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 8 and up |Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Lookout Games , Brown Easy to learn, fast to play, and fraught with surprisingly difficult decisions. The basic premise of putting together a quilt becomes very complex when you're weighing interesting opportunity costs on every single action. At the end of the game, everything boils down to how many buttons you've collected versus how much space on your quilt is unpatched by the time you reach the end of game board with a finite number of spaces. Do I spend a small amount of buttons to fill a large section of my quilt? Do I spend more buttons to fill less quilt with a patch that gives me more income but may move me more towards ending the game too prematurely for victory? Do I not buy any patches, and just advance along the board and collect buttons? It's shockingly complex and interesting considering the simplicity of the mechanics.

I'm a big fan of two player games, as it's great for my wife and I to always have something to do together. This is particularly great for the two of us because set-up is fast and the rules are simple enough that you never waste time referencing the instructions. So we even get to play on busy weeknights.
text_fidelity_b: Patchwork | Strategy / Puzzle Game | Family Board Game | Two Player Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 8 and up |Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Lookout Games , Brown

Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll Since the first Barbie doll was created in 1959, little girl's have always loved to style/color Barbie doll's hair, and this fun to color hair Barbie is no exception. (I took my 1960's ponytail down, so she could look like Sleeping Beauty back in the day!) This gorgeous Color Stylin' Hair Barbie is a huge favorite with the grandchildren now.

Barbie comes with a suction cupped chair, comb, applicator brush, bowl, seven color swatches in 3 colors-3 pink, 2 purple and 2 orange, clip on foiler holder and rubberbands. Barbie is dressed in a glittery pink dress with shoes, necklace and belt. The color application is easy- seat Barbie in her chair, which doesn't move due to an ingenious suction cup bottom, wet the hair section you want to color, place the color swatch in the foiler, then clip the foiler to the wet hair and pull through. When you want to remove the color or color again, you just wash and dry the hair and you are ready for more fun.

There are a couple things you should know before using this coloring set: don't color near carpet, furniture, walls or clothes you don't want to ruin, as these colors can be a permanent stain for certain fabrics or walls. I laid down a cheap plastic tablecloth from the dollar store, so the girls had a great area to play on with no worries. I called Mattel, and found they do not sell extra color swatches, so once these are used up, they are gone, and to replace the colors, you would have to buy another doll. This is a shame, as they always sell accessories and extra hair swatches for the dolls with hair swatches that can be cut, so why not some inexpensive color swatches too Mattel?

The girls just love coloring, braiding and styling the gorgeous streaked areas of this Barbie's hair, so of course they want more colors- and even different colors too. As for something interesting I noticed, I bought another one of these dolls, as I have 2 granddaughters, and we immediately noticed one set colored darkly and another set colored very faintly. I looked closely at the boxes and what did I find on the backs of the boxes, but an expiration date! It says Best Used By and then a date which you need a magnifying glass to read. Reading the back of our boxes showed that one of the boxes colors was expired! That explains the faint color! Being a wonderfully fun to play with Barbie gives this doll 5 Stars, but color that is expired and having no refills brings her down to limited playability with the color, making this gorgeous Barbie a 4 Star doll.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll

Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+ We'd already bought the Sneaky Squirrel Game, which is similar to this game. We've though it was one of the cutest games ever, so we were thrilled to add this one to our collection, too!

With this game, you'll get one of the cutest boxes you've ever seen! (Let me note here that the top and bottom of the game box do NOT fit inside each other. It's the same with the squirrel game.) You'll also get a super cute pair of Shelby tweezers, 4 bowls, a packet of bones, and a double spinner.

Playing the game is pretty simple. There can be up to 4 players at a time. Each player will spin first to see if they will get bones or lose bones or just lose a turn. The second spin is to determine how many bones they will win/lose. If they land on a seagull, it means they will lose bones. If they land on the hungry pug, they get to steal bones from another player. Busy pug means they lose a turn, and landing on the bones mean they win bones for their bowl. They can pick up the bones they win/lose with the tweezers.

The tweezers are a great way to develop motor skills. The game itself is a great, fun way to learn counting skills. My 5 year old is delayed and really struggles with numbers, so I'm always thrilled to find a new, exciting way to teach them to him. This is also a fun game for my 2 year old. It IS pretty simple, so I imagine, on average, 2-4, maybe 5, is probably the best ages for this game.

Overall, this is a super cute game! I can highly recommend this AND the Sneaky Squirrel Game for your young little ones!

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug On the Go Water Wow! Reusable Water-Reveal Activity Cards - Alphabet Letters, Animals - Party Favors, Stocking Stuffers, Toddler Travel Toys, Mess Free Coloring Books For Kids Ages 3+ I ADORE the idea of this kit! It is seriously awesome! There's no clean up whatsoever, so my little ones can "paint" and learn to their heart's content, and I don't have to worry about them staining clothes or painting the walls. If it was designed a bit sturdier, it would be an amazing "busy bag" item(without supervision).

When these cards first came in the mail, I saw that there was a white sticker(of sorts) over the card. Getting this sticker wet makes the picture show up. I knew without supervision, that sticker could be torn up quickly or logged with water. I sat with my boys as they took turns "painting" the cards. They were gentle! Still, as the sticker dried, I saw more and more scratches showing up, which means the picture underneath is no longer hidden(though you can still pretty much see what it's going to be anyway...the white sticker doesn't hide it 100% even with no scratches) I was disappointed that it ended up being so fragile.

I recommend letting your little one have a large space, so that he/she doesn't have to stack the cards together as they dry. We were on the porch the first time my boys used them, and I lay them individually on the porch rail. I stacked them when we came in the house, though. I'm sure that is part of the scratching problem. Unfortunately, that leaves out the places that this kit would come in most handy, like car rides, doctor waiting rooms, and church(for especially young ones). It also makes the key ring that is included pretty worthless.

The little brush is two pieces. You simply unscrew the top, fill it with water, and then put it back together. It worked well, and we didn't have issue with leaking.

Overall, once again, I absolutely adore the idea of this kit, but I wish the cards weren't so fragile.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug On the Go Water Wow! Reusable Water-Reveal Activity Cards - Alphabet Letters, Animals - Party Favors, Stocking Stuffers, Toddler Travel Toys, Mess Free Coloring Books For Kids Ages 3+
